taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes it was formerly placed in Anas (AOU 1983, 1998) and is now treated in Mareca on genetic evidence (AOU 2017).
fieldMarks: Male: bright rusty head with buff crown stripe and mostly gray body
Female very much like female American Wigeon, may have a browner head
Rare hybrids with American Wigeon show intermediate patterns (American Wigeon can also have buff on the crown)
behavior: Reaches North America from both east and west; Pacific-lowland winterers probably come from eastern Siberia
Forages by grazing on land, dabbling, or sometimes submerging head and neck; may steal food brought up by coots or geese; feeds day or night
Piping two-note whistle, seldom heard in America
habitat: Marshes, lakes, bays and fields; in winter often marshy ponds with open ground nearby, flooded fields, shallow coastal estuaries and sheltered bays. American Wigeon presence is the best key to good habitat.
range: Breeds in Eurasia. In North America winters on the Pacific coast from southeastern Alaska to northern Baja California and on the Atlantic-Gulf coast from Labrador and Newfoundland to Florida and southern Texas.

lookalikes.name: American wigeon
lookalikes.howToTell: Female is very much alike; Eurasian may have a browner head. Hybrids are rare and intermediate.
